meta.name: Full Kitaru replays on tau2-bench Telecom: which model holds up?
meta.question: If you swap the model behind a tau2-bench Telecom support agent (or fix its prompt), does it solve more customer tasks end to end, and did Kitaru's cheap step screen predict which swaps would?
meta.domain: Telecom technical support (agent with tools, simulated customer who runs device actions)
meta.who_ran: Hamza Tahir (ZenML), with Claude Code agents

kitaru_details.adapter: kitaru-pydantic-ai 0.3.1 (KitaruAgent) from the same checkout; PydanticAI 2.51.0
kitaru_details.flow: baseline sessions recorded live -> cohort (40 sessions) -> one Kitaru experiment per arm (model override or agent version, explicit passthrough tool policy, evaluator tau2-task-success@1) -> replays run by Kitaru workers

prompt_rewriting.method: Prompt audit (kitaru-model-swap skill, step 2): the policy says to transfer only if a request cannot be handled and to 'try all the possible ways' but never defines when troubleshooting is exhausted. One general rule was appended to the agent instructions: work through every applicable manual section, have the user re-check after each change, check the account side, and transfer only when every step has failed or the manual says to escalate.
prompt_rewriting.leakage_check: Written before any test-split episode ran, from the failure pattern in the public Exgentic recordings (premature transfers) and the tau2 manual's structure; it contains no task ids, scenarios, device states or answers.

setup.tools: tau2's 13 telecom agent tools as PydanticAI tools (schemas from tau2), plus send_message_to_user, whose result is the simulated user's reply. Device tools belong to the simulated user. Kitaru tool policy: explicit passthrough for every tool in every arm (the environment and simulator are local and side-effect free).
setup.user_simulator: tau2's UserSimulator with gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (tau2's default), unchanged across arms.
setup.agent_harness: tau2's own Orchestrator runs each episode; the agent is one PydanticAI run wrapped in KitaruAgent, so one episode is one Kitaru session (tau2_kitaru_agent/episode.py).

judges.name: tau2 evaluator (EvaluationType.ALL; communicate scoring set to tau2's original substring scorer, so grading uses no LLM)
Kitaru evaluator tau2-task-success@1
judges.note: Reads tau2's reward from the episode output; a session with no graded outcome scores 0.

grading.human_agreement_note: No LLM judge, so no human agreement to measure.
grading.self_grading_check_note: No model graded any answer; tau2 grades from environment state.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: correct / n; correct = tau2 reward 1.0. Episodes without a graded outcome count as wrong.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents
metrics.definition: 100 x (sum of agent model cost over all n episodes of the arm, solved or not) / correct. Agent cost is Kitaru's recorded session cost (adapter pricing with cached-input prices) for OpenAI models, and input/cached/output tokens x the unverified table price for open-weight models Kitaru could not price. User-simulator cost is reported separately (user_simulator_cost_usd) and excluded.

metrics.name: paired_vs
metrics.definition: Arm minus reference on the same 40 tasks: mean per-task difference in solved (0/1), in points, with a 95% bootstrap interval (swapbench.stats.paired_delta, tasks resampled, 10000 resamples, seed 0); tasks_gained/lost count flips.

noise.method: GPT-5.2 replayed with no override (noise_gpt-5_2) against its own baseline recording, same 40 tasks.
noise.ci_method: Wilson score 95% for accuracies; per-task bootstrap for paired differences.
noise.tie_threshold_note: A difference whose paired 95% interval includes 0 is reported as not distinguishable.

results_note: One row per (arm, task). Every episode stays in n; episodes without a graded tau2 outcome count as wrong. No episodes were dropped. Replays interrupted by the server restart were retried by Kitaru (attempt 2); each task's final replay is used.

failures.definition: Unsolved episode (tau2 reward 0) in which the agent called transfer_to_human_agents. From the session's tool_call nodes, not text.
failures.example: After several rounds of device checks the agent handed the customer to a human while a fix it could still apply remained.

failures.definition: Unsolved episode (tau2 reward 0) with no transfer_to_human_agents call: the agent ended, or the user simulator ended, with the device or account still in the wrong state. From tool_call nodes.
failures.example: The agent fixed one of the user's problems, the user confirmed the first symptom was gone, and the conversation ended with a second misconfiguration left in place.

failures.definition: The replay or its session failed before tau2 graded the episode (provider error, process failure); counted as unsolved.
failures.example: The candidate's provider returned an error mid-episode and the session failed.

replays_and_step_checks.name: step_screen_vs_full_replay
replays_and_step_checks.description: Does the earlier step check (Kitaru model-swap screen on the public recorded GPT-5.2 calls) rank models the way full replays do? Step agreement is the share of recorded tool choices a candidate repeated; replay accuracy is tau2 task success here.
replays_and_step_checks.note: The step check resent public Exgentic recordings (different harness and user simulator) while replays ran this harness, so this compares rankings, not numbers.

headline_findings.finding: GLM-5.3 solved the most tasks, ahead of the GPT-5.2 baseline on the same 40 tasks.
GPT-5.2 rerun with nothing changed lands on the same accuracy but solves a different set of tasks, which sets the bar for every swap.
The prompt-audit rule (exhaust troubleshooting before transferring) did not measurably help GPT-5.2: its paired difference includes zero and unsolved tasks still ended in a transfer as often.
Models that lost tasks mostly lost them by handing the customer to a human: every unsolved GPT-5.6 Luna episode ended in a transfer.
The cheap step screen did not rank models the way full replays did.

limitations: 40 tasks per arm and one episode per task, so accuracy intervals are wide (about +/-15 points); per-task paired intervals are reported for every comparison.
The user simulator is an LLM (gpt-4.1); the noise arm measures how much outcomes move on a rerun with nothing changed.
Replays start fresh episodes from each task (Kitaru replays the case, not the recorded conversation), so a replay is a new full run, not a step check.
The agent harness is ours (PydanticAI with a send_message_to_user tool), not tau2's built-in LLM agent; numbers are not comparable to the tau2 leaderboard.
Open-weight models ran on one commercial provider through a local router that strips a provider-specific response field; their costs use unverified prices.
Model settings are provider defaults (no reasoning-effort tuning per model).
The step-screen comparison uses different recordings (public Exgentic traces) from the replays.

public_safety.why: Provider names stay private in these exports.
Uses the unmerged model-swap branch; workarounds for kitaru#1339, #1344 and others are described in limitations and meta.

inconsistencies.data: 0.5347 (54/101) in Exgentic's tool_calling harness on the base set vs 0.675 (27/40) here on the test split; different harness, user simulator and task set.

inconsistencies.claim: session.cost is the session's model cost
inconsistencies.data: Sessions of qwen3_8-27b, kimi-k3, glm-5_3, deepseek-v4_1-flash report cost 0 although every llm_call node's cost is null (no price): the rollup counts unpriced calls as 0.
